headline: US-Iran Direct Combat Escalates with Strikes on Nuclear Sites and Air Defenses
subheadline: Iranian missile hit Al Muafaq Saliti Air Base killing two US soldiers in Bahrain.
lede: Direct kinetic engagement between US and Iranian forces escalated today with strikes on Iranian military and nuclear-related sites. The IRGC claims destruction of a US radar installation in Muharraq and a Patriot air defense system in Riffa, Bahrain. US forces targeted capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz and reportedly struck the Bushehr nuclear power plant. An Iranian ballistic missile struck Al Muafaq Saliti Bird Air Base, killing two US soldiers.

sections.title: Russian Gains Near Rai-Oleksandrivka
sections.body: Russian forces advanced near Rai-Oleksandrivka according to DeepStateUA. Ukrainian drones struck seven vessels in the Black and Azov Seas, including three tankers and four cargo ships. Russian forces struck the Eximnefteprodukt plant in Odesa with a Banderol missile, causing a massive fire. The SBU struck a Russian FSB coordination center in Kherson with 13 drones, causing a large fire.

sections.title: US-Iran Strikes Target Nuclear Facilities
sections.body: US forces launched strikes against Iranian military capabilities used against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC Aerospace Force claims destruction of a US radar installation in Muharraq and a Patriot air defense system in Riffa, Bahrain. Reports indicate US strikes targeted the Bushehr nuclear power plant in southern Iran. Kuwaiti air defenses are responding to hostile missile and drone threats with interception sounds reported.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The threat level is extremely high due to direct kinetic strikes between US and Iran, with targeting of nuclear sites and air defense systems indicating significant escalation. Russian forces continue high-intensity aerial strikes using ballistic and cruise missiles against civilian infrastructure and maritime vessels. The potential for unforeseen escalation remains high, as noted by US State Department warnings.
